Current text — identical to 1872 original. Zero textual amendments in 154 years.

case_law.holding_summary: Promissory fraud is actionable in tort independent of contract; state-of-mind is a present fact; reasonable inferences from pleaded facts suffice on demurrer
Present intent not to perform is provable by circumstantial evidence; summary judgment on state of mind is disfavored; survives statute of frauds

case_law.citation: Engalla v. Permanente Medical Group, Inc. (1997) 15 Cal.4th 951
case_law.holding_summary: Fraud analysis applies to adhesive form contracts; pattern of contradiction between representations and internal data supports inference of fraudulent intent
Four independent categories of duty to disclose: fiduciary relationship, partial disclosure, active concealment, exclusive knowledge. Any one triggers § 1572(3) silence-as-fraud.
